name: Emergency ambulance & A&E (category guide)
summary: SCDF 995 vs 1777 private ambulance — free emergency conveyance, non-emergency fees, and why A&E deposits for uninsured foreigners are a hospital billing problem, not an ambulance upsell.
body: Call 995 only for true medical emergencies — SCDF conveys emergency cases to the nearest appropriate MOH hospital without an ambulance fee; since 2019 non-emergency 995 rides are declined or charged if insisted upon. For non-emergencies use a GP/clinic, ride-hail, or the 1777 / private ambulance directory (paid). Arriving by 995 does not skip A&E triage. Uninsured or thinly insured foreigners often face large A&E deposits at private hospitals — ask your insurer for Letter of Guarantee workflows before elective risk, and keep embassy/employer emergency contacts for cash guarantees. Pair ambulance literacy with the emergencies guide (995/999/embassies) and GP/hospital pathway guide. This is a category guide to emergency transport choices, not a ranked private-ambulance company list.
